modes.forge-native: No upstream primary. Forge owns the whole workflow; any upstream entry is a conditional supplemental reference.
modes.hybrid: Forge contract drives; one upstream primary supplies specialist procedure, with evidence-gated overlays.
modes.upstream-powered: An established upstream workflow is the primary procedure for this module's core activity, inside Forge's contracts.

conflicts.rule: Impeccable motion, contrast, and density guidance yields to a proven accessibility requirement.

forgeAuthority: loading, empty, failure, interruption and recovery states
keyboard, semantic, contrast, focus and assistive-technology verification

conflicts.rule: React guidance must not be loaded for Vue, Svelte, Angular, or server-rendered template stacks.
No upstream skill may suppress or downgrade a Forge authorization finding.

forgeAuthority: subject, role, permission, scope, ownership, tenancy and policy model

conflicts.rule: Forge deterministic security analyzers and evidence contracts remain authoritative over any upstream recommendation.
GDPR is a jurisdictional regime, not universal law. It loads only when the repository or the task proves relevance, and never replaces Forge's jurisdiction-neutral analysis.
Forge tenant inference, scope proof, ownership and object-access analysis remain authoritative.
Provider upload convenience guidance never relaxes Forge's content validation, authorization, or storage-ordering requirements.
Provider-specific Supabase sections stay suppressed on plain PostgreSQL; only provider-neutral PostgreSQL guidance applies.

forgeAuthority: generic database design for non-PostgreSQL systems

conflicts.rule: Provider caching guidance yields to Forge privacy and tenancy requirements: no per-user or per-tenant data may be cached under a shared key.

TDD must not demand tests for generated files, documentation-only changes, or repositories that cannot support them. Forge's reasoned applicability model decides; an upstream workflow cannot force a meaningless test.
Sentry is never required for generic Forge observability. Provider-neutral evidence requirements and redaction rules stay Forge-owned.

modules.designation: UPSTREAM_POWERED HYBRID (incident work only; Forge owns backup and restore)

conflicts.rule: The upstream debugging workflow covers live incident investigation only. It never leads backup, restore, RPO/RTO, or regional-failover work: the Forge recovery contract owns those, and an untested backup remains NOT_VERIFIED recovery capability regardless of any upstream procedure.

forgeAuthority: recovery point and recovery time objectives

conflicts.rule: No external deployment happens without explicit user approval. Provider deployment guidance describes a procedure; it never authorises running it.

forgeAuthority: approval boundary for external side effects

conflicts.rule: Google Cloud guidance must not be applied to AWS, Railway, Fly, or on-premises targets, and Cloudflare guidance must not be applied to non-Cloudflare hosting.

forgeAuthority: the distinction between measured and estimated cost

conflicts.rule: No provider house writing style is imposed on Forge users; Vercel's writing-guidelines skill is deliberately not imported.
A provider skill activates only when that provider is detected or explicitly requested; it never supplies the generic payment model.
forge-all orchestrates the Forge module graph. It must never delegate routing to an upstream provider's router, bootstrap, or command set.

Forge's independent, fail-closed Ship gate is authoritative. No upstream completion checklist, command router, or branch-completion workflow may declare a release ready, and subjective UI advisories never block Ship.
